title: Research best-effort F_5 packed encoding
description:
Prototype 2–4 candidate $\mathbb{F}_5$ packed encodings, measure cycles/op for each, and produce a decision document selecting the winning candidate that the implementation phase will instantiate.

## Background

⚠ **User approval required** before selecting the winning encoding — this is the input contract for the $\mathbb{F}_5$ implementation work.

The bipedal $\mathbb{F}_3$ encoding minimises bitwise op counts (2 ops/mul, 6 ops/add) by using a 4-state alphabet with one redundant codeword. $\mathbb{F}_5$ has 5 elements; the simplest baseline is 3-bit-per-element packed (one redundant codeword in 8 states, 16 elements per `u64`) with a $2^{16}$-entry table-LUT for mul. Better encodings may exist by exploiting the multiplicative structure ($\mathbb{F}_5^*$ is cyclic of order 4 — log/sign split is plausible).

This issue prototypes 2–4 candidate encodings in `dev/research/f5_packing/` (mirroring `dev/research/rns_prototype/`), measures cycles/op for each on synthetic workloads, and produces a decision document selecting the winning candidate.

Hard fallback if no novel encoding beats the LUT baseline by $\ge 1.5\times$: select the 3-bit + LUT baseline. The fallback is acceptable; document it as the chosen encoding in the decision doc.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `dev/research/f5_packing/` exists and builds with `cargo build -p f5-packing-prototype --release`.
- [ ] [hard] At least 2 candidate encodings are implemented and benchmarked.
- [ ] [hard] `dev/plans/r1_f5_encoding_decision.md` exists and is attached via `jit doc add`, naming the winning candidate with measured cycles/op.
- [ ] [hard] The decision doc documents the bitwise op counts for `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div` on the chosen encoding.
- [ ] [hard] The user has signed off on the chosen encoding (recorded as a comment) before transitioning to `done`.
